title: CmdPal: Extension SDK 0.12.260812002 can't be used with project using old .NET versions
author: jiripolasek
summary: The CmdPal Extension SDK 0.12.260812002 package is reported to force .NET 10 into older-target extension projects, and source packaging evidence shows a plausible target-framework mismatch.

status.label: Design investigation queued
status.detail: Repository packaging evidence is enough for a maintainer-side design pass; a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP would not answer the SDK target-framework question.

next_action.label: Queue SDK packaging design
next_action.reason: Verify the shipped NuGet assets/dependencies and define the supported extension target framework.

judgment.rationale: This is a credible 0.101-era SDK packaging compatibility issue rather than a generic user environment report. The author is a collaborator and removed automated author-feedback labels after the bot asked for irrelevant app diagnostics.
evidence: The issue names Command Palette Extension SDK 0.12.260812002 and states that it forces .NET 10 onto projects using older .NET versions.
The author is a repository collaborator and twice removed Needs-Author-Feedback after the bot request.
The current repo-wide CoreTargetFramework is net10.0 and the extension template targets net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a full packaging design that verifies the actual packed assembly target, aligns NuGet framework folders/dependencies, and documents the oldest supported extension target.

issue_context.summary: A CmdPal SDK package version associated with 0.101 is not usable by older .NET extension projects because it appears to introduce .NET 10 requirements.
known_information: The report targets SDK version 0.12.260812002 and PowerToys 0.101.
The author is a collaborator and removed the irrelevant Needs-Author-Feedback label twice.
The report concerns NuGet package consumption by extension projects, not local PowerToys runtime behavior.
No assignee, linked fix, or duplicate is present.
inferences: The package may be shipping net10-built assemblies or dependencies under net8 metadata, but the actual produced nupkg still needs verification.
issue_context.analysis: The next decision is engineering-owned: whether the SDK should support older target frameworks and how the package should express that support. Reporter diagnostics would not materially change that decision.
initial_investigation: src/Common.Dotnet.props currently sets CoreTargetFramework to net10.0.
